title: Status controversiae: are any sins non-excluding and non-deserving of eternal death by nature?
source_text: LXIII. Itaque id solum in controversia manet; inter Scholam Romanam & Theo-logos Protestantes, An sint quaedam peccata quae natura sua Dei gratiam non exclu-dant, nec aeternam mortem mereantur, & propter quae sola Deus non posset juste hominem abjicere, & ab amicitia sua in aeternum & prorsus repellere, si rigide cum eo agere vellet? Quod communiter affirmant Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae; Protestantes vero negant.
pass_a_gloss: And so this alone remains in controversy between the Roman School and Protestant theologians: Whether there are certain sins which by their nature do not exclude God’s grace, nor merit eternal death, and on account of which alone God could not justly cast a man away and forever and utterly repel him from his friendship, if he wished to deal rigidly with him? Which the Doctors of the Roman Church commonly affirm; but Protestants deny.
pass_b_english: The live quarrel narrows to one question: sins venial by nature—non-excluding, non-deserving eternal death even under rigid right?

choices.why: Status controversiae distilled after shared ground.
